newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Unilever still not using soya in margarine.
newsitem.headline: German Unilever still not using soya in margarine.

text.p: The German subsidiary of Anglo-Dutch Unilever will continue to use alternatives to soy oil in margarine as long as a row over genetically altered soybeans remains unresolved, it said on Thursday.
Manfred Stach, the chairman of the board of Unilever GmbH, said the company believed the new type of soya was safe and was bowing to pressure from opponents to genetically altered organisms (GMOs).
His remarks were made during a briefing on company results for 1996.
Unilever supported a comprehensive labelling system for food products containing (GMOs), Stach said.
Oppponents, led by environmental group Greenpeace, say too little is known about GMOs and more time is needed to study their possible effect on human health and the environment.
Unilever did not believe a separation of transgenic soybeans and conventional ones was possible and because of its limited market share felt unable to exert pressure on U.S. producers, Stach said.
The company buys some 120,000 tonnes of oil a year and, in its German oils, fats and margarine production, has replaced soy oil with rapeseed and sunseed oils since last autumn.
Unilever GmbH in 1996 raised its share in German margarine sales (by value) by 0.8 percent to 56 percent.
Its total food sales dropped by two percent in value last year to 6.9 billion marks, largely a result of lower ice cream sales in a cold summer.
The firm also sells cosmetics, detergents and chemicals.
